title: Project adapter
description: How the pipeline sets up, smoke-checks and validates a project (<live root>/adapters/<id>.yaml). Setup, smoke and local validation commands run in their own process group: when a command returns, normally or by timeout, nothing it started is left in that group. A command that leaves the group (setsid, a daemon) is unsupported, and nothing sweeps what it leaves behind.

commands.description: Setup commands run on a clean worktree.

ci.description: Where validation runs. 'local' needs a command, 'none' must be justified by 'missing'.

command.description: Local validation command, required when ci is 'local'.

missing.description: What the gate could not cover, e.g. ['tests']. Required when ci is 'none'.

required_checks.description: GitHub check names the gate judges by, e.g. ['test']. Matches an Actions check-run name or a legacy commit status context. Only meaningful when ci is 'github'; without it the gate judges by every check on the sha.

e2e.description: An e2e GitHub Actions workflow the dispatcher dispatches once per code-card candidate SHA, after green CI and a green (or skipped) review and before the card becomes releasable (docs/PROTOCOLS.md 'E2E stage'), or, with placement after_merge, on main after the merge. Needs ci 'github'. The run is identified from GitHub's dispatch answer (return_run_details), so the workflow needs no extra input.

workflow.description: The workflow file name (e.g. e2e.yml) or its numeric id in the project's repository.

inputs.description: Static workflow_dispatch inputs sent with every dispatch.

deadline.description: How long the run may take before the card is Blocked with deadline_passed, e.g. 90m or 6h. Default 6h.

candidate_input.description: The workflow_dispatch input that receives the candidate SHA, when the workflow takes one.

dispatch_id_input.description: Optional: the workflow_dispatch input that receives the dispatcher's dispatch id. When declared, crash recovery attaches only a run whose run-name carries it. No static input and not candidate_input may share its name.

placement.description: Where the stage runs. before_merge (the default): on each code card's candidate, before it becomes releasable. after_merge: for a workflow that can only run on a commit whose releases the post-merge CI of main published; cards merge with no e2e, and once a merge commit's post-merge CI is green the dispatcher runs the workflow on main, on a branch it owns (pipeline-e2e/<dispatch id>) pointed at the newest green merge SHA, covering every card merged since the last run, with at most one run in flight per project (docs/PROTOCOLS.md 'After merge'). candidate_input then receives that SHA.

write_project_files.description: Whether the pipeline may write files into the project repo.

broad_check.description: The project's own broad suite: which module `check broad --module` runs, which package that run must import, and optionally which interpreter runs it. `additionalProperties: false` is why an unknown key here is refused outright, so this block has to describe the whole contract. Declaring it is mandatory for a project that gets cards: an adapter without it is refused as `broad_check_not_declared` and its cards block at preflight (issue:81a0a1e5c15225fa360e). It is not `required` here, because a missing contract is a fact about the project rather than a malformed adapter, and refusing it as `adapter_invalid` would hide which of the two is wrong.

interpreter.description: Optional adapter-owned interpreter for module broad checks. A relative path is resolved from the candidate workspace, for example .venv/bin/python; that .venv remains exclusively adapter-owned. Omitted, the check runs on the interpreter that runs the wrapper, which dispatcher-launched workers receive from .ummanu-task-env/venv. The subprocess also prepends the candidate import roots and records the actual interpreter and import origin.

import_package.description: Package the check process must import and prove came from the candidate workspace.

module.description: The module a `python -m` runs: this project's broad suite. Without it nobody but the project itself could say which suite a broad check means, and the worker prompt had to print a placeholder. Not required by the schema, so an adapter written before this key existed is not suddenly malformed, and PR #331 stopped the contract layer refusing such a block too: omitting it means only that the caller has to name the suite itself, which `check broad`/`check show` with no `--module` reports as `no_broad_check_module`.

args.description: The exact argument vector passed after the module. Kept as a list, never a rendered string, because `-k a b` and `-k 'a b'` render identically while running different checks.

local.description: Local membership is either the validated Ummanu CI manifest or owned by the declared broad runner. Runner selectors append to broad_check.args, with the declared separator; no discovery fallback.

selector_args.description: Empty for native positional selectors (pytest); ["--"] for the shared launcher interface. Appended after broad_check.args only on subset runs.
